newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili drifts east, pounds central Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili drifts east, pounds central Cuba.

text.p: Hurricane Lili drifted to the east as it pounded west-central Cuba on Friday with sustained 90 mph (145 kph) winds and torrential rains, the National Hurricane Center said.
The eye of the storm remained just south of the Cuba coast but a broad area of its leading edge had moved onshore, forecasters said.
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the center of Lili was located at latitude 22.4, longitude 81.1 west, about 50 miles (80 km) south-southeast of Varadero, Cuba.

Forecasters said the storm had moved to the east at about 9 mph (15 kph) during the last few hours but was expected to resume an east-northeast track later Friday, with the eye emerging off Cuba's north coast Friday evening.

The storm's top winds were likely to fluctuate as it moved over land, forecasters said. Sustained winds of 92 mph (147 kph) with gusts to 115 (185 kph) were measured early Friday at Cayo Largo del Sur, near the south coast of central Cuba.
A hurricane warning remained in effect for Cuba's mainland from Camaguey province westward, but was discontinued for the Isle of Youth.
The government of the Bahamas issued a hurricane warning for the central Bahamas, the hurricane center said. A hurricane warning for the northwest Bahamas remained in effect.
A tropical storm warning remained in effect for the Florida Keys from Key Largo to the Dry Tortugas including Florida Bay, but was likely to be discontinued later Friday.
Hurricane-force winds extended outward up to 85 miles (135 km) from the center and tropical storm-force winds extended out about 145 miles (230 km).
The storm threatened to dump up to 12 inches (30 cm) of rain in its path, raising the possibility of life-threatening flash floods and mudslides in mountainous areas, forecasters said.
It also threatened storm surge flooding of three to six feet (1-2 meters), particularly near and to the east of where the center crosses the coast, forecasters said.
